subject: Request: Certification of Dataflow for UK Addendum & Third-Party Processors
messages:
From: Dr. Sophie Kramer <sophie.kramer@medisoft.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medisoft.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dataflow certification for UK Addendum & subprocessors

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement review for Medisoft’s UK launch, our legal/security team needs confirmation on two things before we sign the DPA addendum:

1) A mapping of where customer data that originates in the UK may traverse (regions, subprocessors, any U.S. destinations) and which transfer safeguards will apply (SCCs, UK IDTA/UK Addendum, or other TIAs).
2) Evidence our subprocessors who will process UK-origin data have controls aligned with the UK addendum (attestations, certificates, or SOC2 + configurations).

I’ve attached a preliminary mapping (medisoft_initial_mapping.xlsx) that shows the flows we expect. Can Redwood certify the flows and provide the subprocessor evidence or a timeline for delivery? We’re targeting signing the DPA addendum by Aug 10 and need to know if this is feasible.

Also include any recommended clause language if there are conditional routing or onshore/offshore exceptions you require.

Appreciate a short turnaround here — can you confirm next steps and owners?

Best,
Sophie
Dr. Sophie Kramer
Head of Security, Medisoft Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Sophie Kramer <sophie.kramer@medisoft.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dataflow certification for UK Addendum & subprocessors

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask and for the mapping.

Quick notes / proposed plan:
- We can provide a signed statement of where data is processed and a subprocessor inventory exported as CSV (I’m attaching a preliminary export).
- For legal-level certification (SCCs / UK Addendum applicability) we need the Privacy team + Legal to confirm the right label for each flow (e.g., SCCs vs UK IDTA vs other contractual safeguards). I’m looping in Priya (Privacy) and Karthik (Legal) to own those calls.
- Timeline: Privacy can produce a control evidence packet + inventory in ~4 business days; Legal needs to review the Medisoft mapping and propose any redlines to the addendum language within 5–7 business days. If both are on that cadence, we should be able to meet your Aug 10 target.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_inventory.csv (snapshot), and I asked Priya to prep an SCCs/UK-addendum reconciliation.

Can you confirm which data categories on your sheet are "personal data" vs "pseudonymized / analytics" — helps us prioritize controls evidence for high-risk flows. Also, would you prefer DocuSign for the signed statement or a PDF from Legal? We can do either.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0121

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Sophie Kramer <sophie.kramer@medisoft.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dataflow certification for UK Addendum & subprocessors

Hi Sophie — looping in with a technical/controls readout and next steps.

Short answers up front: for the flows in the spreadsheet, Redwood intends to apply either SCCs or the UK Addendum depending on the legal basis and routing. Where requests come from the UK and data strictly remains within EU/UK regions we will not rely on alternate safeguards. For any flows that transit the U.S. (e.g., S3 backup, metrics ingestion, support debugging sessions) we will map to SCCs + additional contractual clauses or a documented TIA category.

What I will deliver (ETA: 4 business days from today):
- A per-flow reconciliation document mapping medisoft_initial_mapping.xlsx -> transfer safeguard (SCCs / UK Addendum / TIA) and required evidence type.
- Subprocessor attestations where we have vendor-provided certificates; if a subprocessors only has SOC2 but not a specific UK attestation, we’ll provide control matrices showing equivalence.
- A short playbook on conditional routing options (pin to EU region, on-prem agents, limited support access) and the operational cost/latency implications.

Questions for Medisoft:
- Which categories in column C of your spreadsheet are considered "special category" or health-sensitive? Call those out so we can mark them high priority.
- Does Medisoft require a prior written approval step for any new subprocessor that will process UK-origin data? If yes, we’ll include the approval workflow in the addendum appendix.

Attachments we’re sharing now: redwood_sccs_matrix.pdf (overview). I’ll send the per-flow reconciliation and attestations as a follow-up link.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai | +1 510-555-0184

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Sophie Kramer <sophie.kramer@medisoft.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dataflow certification for UK Addendum & subprocessors

Sophie / team — quick legal clarifications and a request from our side.

1) Redlines: We will only sign the addendum once we’ve validated the per-flow mapping. If Medisoft has highly prescriptive routing clauses that require on-shore-only processing for analytics or backups, we will need to evaluate operational impact and propose limited carve-outs. Please highlight any routing clauses you consider non-negotiable.

2) Evidence scope: For subprocessors we can provide (a) vendor attestations, (b) SOC2 reports via NDA, and (c) our control matrices. If Medisoft requires raw audit logs for subprocessors, we will require a narrow scope and an agreement on retention and access controls before sharing.

3) DocuSign & sign-off: Marissa — once Priya posts the reconciliation, we suggest Redwood prepares: (i) a short signed statement confirming our inventory & processing locations, and (ii) an appendix listing subprocessors with links to attestations. We can put both in DocuSign and share with Medisoft’s signatories. Sophie — is your procurement team OK with a two-step sign-off (operational reconciliation first, then legal sign-off in DocuSign)?

If that works, we should be able to lock in language within 5 business days after we receive the clarified columns for special categories.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
